text: Empirical studies find that depressed patients consistently overestimate the duration of intervals — a result consistent with the phenomenological report that in depression time seems to slow, or even to stop.
explanation: This is true. Depressed patients consistently overestimate interval duration — time 'passes slowly' — which fits the reported experience of time thickening or stopping and is explained by increased self-monitoring feeding the attentional-gate mechanism, so that more clock pulses accumulate. This is the mirror image of mania, where patients underestimate duration and time seems to accelerate.
